title: The Sneeze-Pee Face-Off

format_analysis.format: AI 3D talking-character duet, Miro #117: a Pixar-style panty liner and the plain black underwear square up like boxers on a bed under a strap, then trade form-only lines. Every line hops to a new angle or a new place (handbag, drawer, bin, washing line), with real-look product inserts and two boxing-poster freezes. It's the same two characters as V2-a and V2-b. It runs as an off-proof test cell (the script's own flag).
format_analysis.how_it_should_look: Pixar-quality 3D characters composited into photoreal sets (the 1691171645641479 / 1700150534480418 look), never a cartoon world. Warm practical light: a 2700K lamp plus soft window fill, bright and readable at thumbnail size, nothing dark. Shallow depth of field (35-50mm look). Smooth dolly pushes and low/high/OTS angles, plus edit punch-ins (115-125%) on emphasis words; gens upscaled to 4K so the punch-ins stay sharp. The palette is built into the sets: Warm Cream duvet, Claret throw, Blush pillows, tan tote, cream tiles. Never pastel-clinical, never a hotel or hospital bed. The liner is clean white with no stains; the underwear is matte black and true to the sample photos. Captions: the hook is a Claret pill with cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold; body captions and form labels are Plum Ink on Warm Cream boxes at ~42-58% height. Posters use Hanken ExtraBold caps on Plum Ink bands. Fraunces appears only on the end-card brand line. Sound bed: a dry, upbeat comedy bed (pizzicato + brushed snare) under a boxing-bell motif (ding at 0.3s, ding-ding on both posters), with a foley gag on every cut in the first 10s (achoo, bell, crowd ooh, zip, sticky thwack, drawer thunk, elastic fwip).
format_analysis.runtime_main: 33.0s with every locked line kept. The script's ~28s doesn't fit its 80 spoken words. The proposed trims T1+T2 bring it to ~30.1s, and T1-T3 to ~29.0s (see pacing_check.vo_fit_issues).
format_analysis.aspect: 9:16 (4:5-safe); all text between ~14% and ~62% height inside the centre 4:5 crop
format_analysis.build_profile: 0-11.7s: on-camera characters, one speaker per clip, the non-speaker silent with mouth closed. Bed set (wide, low-angle hero, punch-in), the poster freeze, and two location hops (handbag = liner, drawer = underwear). 11.7-15.6s: faceless real-look inserts (hands stretch the waistband; an AI woman pulls leggings on, side-on), with the underwear's voice off-screen, so no lip-sync. 15.6-24.8s: the liner's confession on 3 bed angles (high, ECU, OTS), then the bin hop. 24.8-27.0s: a real washer flash, then the underwear on the washing line. 27.0-29.1s: the truce two-shot, then the poster reprise. 29.1-33.0s: the brand end card with both characters small in the corners. Voices: two ElevenLabs Voice Design voices shared across V2-a/b/c. LP_LINER is higher, fussy and fast; LP_UNDIES is warm, dry and unhurried. Both are women ~30-35, accent per launch market (Nikita to OK). Record the whole two-voice dialogue first as one timed track, cut the animatic to it, and slice per clip. Per-clip voice path: Veo 3.1 native line, then ElevenLabs Voice Changer, for two-face or action-heavy clips (S1, S5-S6, S11, S12, S14-S15, S17, S18, end-card corners). ElevenLabs line first, then audio-driven lip-sync on a closed-mouth base, for the 3 held single-face close-ups (S3-S4, S7-S8, S13). ElevenLabs only for off-screen lines (S2, S9, S10, S16, S19). Never single-track lip-sync two faces.

reference_ads.what_we_take: The frame-1 grammar exactly: a strap across the top over two characters side by side on a warm-lamp bed, pad left and black underwear right, with the underwear's face on its upper front panel and boxed captions mid-frame. NOT its pacing: it sits on one bed angle for ~14s, averages 4.8s per shot and has 2 cuts in 3-10s. NOT its copy: it uses an absolute leak claim, a 100 ml figure and a pour demo at ~20s, all banned for us. Only its frame-1 layout is borrowed (it's 180 days live but not in its page's top 30/40).

Every line moves the talking character to a new room or angle (living room, vanity, bedroom, kitchen, bedside) and changes its size cut to cut. That's our hop on every line (handbag, drawer, bin, washing line), plus the 'honest confession' register for the liner's self-roast. Its word-by-word captions become our 2-4 word boxes.

Each object lives in its own real place (marble counter, tub edge, washing machine). That gives us the handbag/drawer/bin/washing-line sets, a caption pill per phrase, and the liner owning its own form flaws ('I bunch up, shift out of place'). NOT its ~7s single-speaker holds (ours cap at 3.0s) and NOT its claims.

Text-hook anchor (Everdries video #27, 169 days, top 3.6% of ~740): the 'X VS Y / WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE?' strap. Our VS roundel, our 1.6s 'What's the difference?' bridge and alternate 1 are built on it.

recommended.text: Big sneeze. Little pee.  [+ VS roundel at 0.3s]  ->  1.6s: What's the difference?
recommended.on_screen_timing: 0.0s-3.0s pill 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' (on at frame 0). 0.3s-3.0s VS roundel. 1.6s-3.0s box 'What's the difference?' (re-captioned when spoken at 5.0s). 3.0s-3.8s the locked title 'THE SNEEZE-PEE FACE-OFF' on the boxing-poster freeze, reprised at 28.0s as 'HER CALL.'
recommended.style: Hook pill: Claret #A33154 with cream #F5EDE6 Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, 2 lines, ~7% of frame height per line, centred at ~20-28% height where the 1691171645641479 strap sits, above both characters' heads. VS roundel: Plum Ink disc with a Claret ring and cream 'VS', ~12% of frame width, between the fighters at ~38-44%. Bridge: Warm Cream box with Plum Ink text at ~52-58%. Poster title: cream Hanken ExtraBold caps on a Plum Ink band at ~16-22%. Everything inside the centre 4:5 crop.
recommended.why: 5 words read in the first 1.5s (cap 7). The text carries the moment and the visual carries the matchup: two fighters, a bell and a VS badge read 'versus' without words, so the text spends its budget on the sneeze + pee. That's the ICP filter for 30-45, and it means a muted stranger can't read a panty liner on frame 1 as period content. It's built on the trigger-moment proof for 30-45 (AD_RESEARCH A7: Origin 'Leak when you sneeze?' 372 days, 'Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs' 112 days, Everdries 'sneeze' ~100 live), and the bridge is the proven open loop of Everdries #27 / Carol #10. Why the locked stack doesn't win as written: (1) it reads 8 words in the first 1.5s; (2) the title and the strap are both specced at ~18-19% height, so they collide; (3) the title is in Fraunces, which the brief keeps for the end-card brand line; (4) 'sneeze' and 'pee' get said twice; (5) 'FACE-OFF' has no proven anchor. On the 3.0s poster the title gets read alone and becomes a free re-hook at the first cut.

alternates.text: Panty liner vs underwear: what's the difference?
alternates.why: 7 words. The X-VS-Y strap of the duet ref names both fighters and puts the locked open loop in the same read. Risk: it doesn't name the moment, so a liner on frame 1 can read as period content. Better as the B-test or for retargeting, where she already knows the moment.
alternates.proven_anchor: Everdries #27 'DIAPERS VS EVERDRIES Boyshort / WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE?' (945622924750214, 169 days, top 3.6% of ~740); Carol Henderson #10 'OLD VS NEW EVERDRIES' + spoken 'Old versus new Everdries, what's the difference?' (895402959657367, 275 days); UltraDries 1691171645641479 strap 'Disposable Pad Vs ULTRADRIES Underwear' (180 days).

alternates.text: Sneeze-pee: panty liner vs underwear  ->  1.5s: What's the difference?
alternates.why: 5 words, then 3. It merges the moment and the matchup into one strap read, labels both cartoons for a muted viewer, and keeps the strap layout of the duet ref. It loses the rhythm of 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' Best single-strap option if Nikita wants the fighters named on frame 1.
alternates.proven_anchor: 1691171645641479 'X Vs Y' strap (180 days) + Everdries #27 'WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE?' (169 days, top 3.6%) + the sneeze moment (Origin 'Leak when you sneeze?', 372 days).

alternates.text: Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs.
alternates.why: 6 words over the same VS stand-off. It's the strongest 30-45 proof in the research and passes Meta's personal-attributes rule as written (AD_RESEARCH §3). Flag: next to the underwear it implies the underwear changes the sneeze outcome (an implied performance promise), so run it only after the founder wear test logs the sneeze.
alternates.proven_anchor: Pelvic-clinic hook 'Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs.' (112 days, AD_RESEARCH §3, proven on 30-45 women).

text_hook.note: DIFFERS FROM THE LOCKED SCRIPT; Nikita chiefs it. (1) 'THE SNEEZE-PEE FACE-OFF' moves off frame 1 to the 3.0s boxing-poster freeze, in Hanken not Fraunces. (2) A VS roundel graphic is added at 0.3s. (3) 'What's the difference?' keeps its 1.6s slot and is re-captioned when spoken at 5.0s. To run the locked stack instead and still hit 7 words: drop 'THE' -> 'SNEEZE-PEE FACE-OFF' (3 words, band at 14-18%) + 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' (4 words, pill at 22-28%), both in Hanken.

visual_hook_build.miro: #117 3D Talking Character (two-character standoff under a strap, the grammar of UltraDries 1691171645641479)
visual_hook_build.frame_1: 9:16, bright and warm. Camera at duvet height on a Warm Cream duvet (Claret throw on the foot edge, Blush pillows, a soft-focus headboard, a lamp glowing top-right). LEFT: the clean white panty-liner character, mid-shove, leaning ~15 deg into the underwear with a motion smear on its edge. RIGHT: the plain black underwear character (from the 5 sample photos), upright on its leg openings, tilted ~8 deg away mid-rock, face on the upper front panel just under the waistband, one brow starting to lift. Both are ~35% of frame height and centred inside the 4:5 safe area. The Claret pill 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' is already on at ~20-28% above their heads, with the tiny AI label at ~60%. No person, no brands, no text inside the generated image.
build_steps: 1. UNBLOCK THE PRODUCT: Nikita shoots the 5 CJ sample photos (flat front, flat back, side, stretched, under black leggings; daylight, neutral backdrop) and uploads them to Higgsfield as reference media. Every underwear frame, the character included, copies rise, waistband width, leg line and matte sheen from them. Never prompt the garment from text or from NUMBER_SHEET §13 (that's the old lace product).

2. SHARED CHARACTER ANCHORS (one set for V2-a/V2-b/V2-c, matching the spec in the V2-b board; generate once, approve once, register as Higgsfield/Kling reference elements LP_LINER and LP_UNDIES). LP_LINER: a slim, softly rounded, wingless-silhouette panty liner (~2-3mm thin) with a quilted micro-dimple top sheet, pure clean white, and a pale-mint unbranded peel strip on the back (V2-c's 'sticks on' gag peels it). Big glossy round eyes in the top third, small brows, a mouth at mid-body, and two small soft tab-hands from the sides (cartoon arms, not pad wings). It hops and bends at the middle. True scale is ~55-60% of the underwear's height. NEVER stains, yellowing, show-through, brand marks or a villain face. LP_UNDIES: the real plain black underwear standing upright on its leg openings. Two calm oval eyes with soft white sclera and a Rose Taupe lid line, sitting one finger-width below the waistband seam. A small dry mouth that ends ABOVE the line where the leg openings curve in. The gusset zone stays blank and is never the face. Brows are fabric creases (the one-brow lift is its signature). No arms: it moves by waistband shrugs, folding nods, leans and hops. Each sheet: turnaround (front, 3/4, side, back) plus expressions (liner: eager, fussy, deflated, sheepish, wry; underwear: deadpan, brow-lift, dry half-smile, contented).

3. BEDROOM PLATE (scene-lock, V2-c only): Nano Banana Pro, 9:16, 2k, empty set. Camera at duvet height, 35mm look, f/2.8. Warm Cream duvet with soft folds filling the lower half, a folded Claret throw on the foot edge, Blush and cream pillows, a soft-focus wooden headboard, a lamp glowing top-right (2700K), soft window fill from the left. An adult's bedroom: no brands, no titled books, no toys, nothing clinical. Every bed angle (wide, low hero, high, ECU, OTS, truce) is generated from this plate so the set never changes.

4. HOOK START FRAME (F1-DUO-wide = frame 0 of the motion): on the approved plate with both elements, compose the pose from frame_1 with mouths CLOSED and headroom above for the pill. Check it at phone size with the pill, VS roundel and AI label mocked on top.

5. ANIMATE FROM MID-MOTION: Veo 3.1 start-frame, 8s gen, keep 0.0-3.0s. Motion beats: the shove lands and the underwear springs back upright (0.0-0.4s); on the bell both bounce into a boxer's stance, the liner on its toes with tab-hands up like gloves and the underwear planted with one brow up (0.3-1.0s); slow dolly push-in 100->112% while the liner leans toward the lens on 'sneeze' (1.0-3.0s); the underwear's eyes slide to the liner at ~2.7s. Only the liner speaks. Start the edit 4-8 frames into the gen so the published frame 0 is already moving. If Veo eases in from rest, use Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame (end = both in stance) to force the trajectory.

6. BELL + SFX (editor): 0.1s muffled off-screen 'achoo' (audio only, no person, and the underwear must NOT react to it). 0.3s single boxing-bell DING locked to the stance bounce. The comedy bed enters on the bell. A whoosh under the push-in. Duck or strip Veo's own ambience.

7. TITLE STRAP + TEXT (editor only, never inside a prompt): the 0.0s Claret pill 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' sits in the strap slot of 1691171645641479; the VS roundel slams in at 0.3s on the bell; the 1.6s box reads 'What's the difference?'; the AI label is persistent. The locked title 'THE SNEEZE-PEE FACE-OFF' is built as the 3.0s boxing-poster freeze: a Claret | Warm Cream split with a Plum Ink divider, the two poster-pose stills cut out (remove_background), the VS roundel, name plates 'PANTY LINER' | 'UNDERWEAR', and a 4-frame slam with a white flash. It's reprised at 28.0s with the band flipped to 'HER CALL.'

8. VOICE PATH: design LP_LINER and LP_UNDIES in ElevenLabs (shared V2-a/b/c), then record the whole dialogue as one timed two-voice track before any video gen and cut the animatic to it. For the hook (two faces + heavy body motion): Veo native line on the liner only, then ElevenLabs Voice Changer onto LP_LINER, which keeps Veo's lip timing. Audio-driven lip-sync is risky with two faces because the tool may animate the wrong one. Held single-face close-ups (S3-S4, S7-S8, S13): closed-mouth base clip + audio-driven lip-sync. Off-screen lines: ElevenLabs only. Test the hook clip both ways (script Q2) before batching.

9. ANGLE LIBRARY + HOPS (change angle or place on every line, like 1400650075258672): F1-DUO-wide (hook + truce), F6-UNDIES-lowangle (hero, lamp halo), F7-LINER-highangle (deflated), F4-LINER-ecu (gags), F8-DUO-ots (across the duvet over the underwear's waistband), plus the boxing-poster split freeze (editor, twice). Location hops land on the words that name a place: 'in her bag' -> inside a tan tote (S5-S6), 'in the drawer' -> an open underwear drawer (S7-S8), 'the trash' -> a bathroom pedal bin (S14-S15), 'the wash' -> a washer flash + the washing line (S16-S17). Edit punch-ins of 115-120% land on 'difference', the 'sticks on' slap and 'drawer'. No angle ever repeats on consecutive lines, and no angle holds longer than 3.0s.
visual_hook_build.lane_and_tool: AI start frame + motion: Nano Banana Pro on Higgsfield (9:16, 2k, LP_LINER + LP_UNDIES reference elements on the bedroom plate) for the start frame, then Veo 3.1 start-frame (8s, native audio) for the hook, with Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame as the motion fallback. ElevenLabs for the two designed voices + Voice Changer. CapCut for the pill, VS roundel, poster freeze, push-in, punch-ins and SFX. Every tool is a recommendation; the generator isn't confirmed by Nikita.
visual_hook_build.fallback: (a) If Veo animates both mouths, breaks the scale between the characters, or won't hold the underwear's face position in the two-shot: generate each character separately on the same bedroom plate (Kling 3.0 + its element, left and right halves), composite them in the editor, and fake the shove with a 6-frame bump + 2-frame shake + whoosh; lip-sync the liner only. (b) If the 5 CJ photos aren't in yet: build and approve LP_LINER, the bedroom plate and the liner-only shots (S5-S6, S11, S12, S14-S15) now. Use the CJ listing images only for a non-publishable pipeline test of the underwear. Nothing showing the underwear ships until it's rebuilt from the real photos. (c) If a face on fabric won't lip-sync (face not detected), switch that clip to Veo native + Voice Changer.
failure_modes_to_reject: Underwear face at or near the gusset/crotch, or below the leg-opening curve line; any anatomy or 'worn by a body' read on the cartoon underwear.
Garment drift from the sample photos: lace, a logo, extra seams or a gusset line, the wrong rise or waistband width, a shiny/latex sheen, or a grey/brown/navy tint.
Any stain, yellowing, coloured fluid or 'used' look on the liner; wings that make it read as a thick maxi pad; brand print; the liner oversized (above ~65% of the underwear's height) or toy-tiny.
Both mouths moving in a one-speaker clip; lip flap on the silent character; Veo inventing a narrator, a third voice or its own music.
A static or eased-in frame 0 (characters standing still), or a dark/underexposed first frame.
The shove reading as violent (a punch or hit) rather than a playful shoulder bump; real boxing gloves; a referee, belt, KO, scorecard or raised hand (anything that declares a winner).
A human, a hand or a child entering any character shot; toddler-toy styling instead of adult Pixar comedy; human teeth or uncanny lips on the underwear; arms on the underwear.
A bedroom that reads as a hotel/hospital, a pastel-clinical palette, real brand marks (bedding, tote, keys, washer badge, bin), or titled books.
Character drift between clips: eye size or colour, liner proportions, the underwear's rise or face position.
Text generated inside any frame (all text is added in the editor).

shots.angle_or_room: Bedroom duvet, camera at duvet height (eye level with the characters), 35mm look, f/2.8. Lamp bokeh top-right. This is the 1691171645641479 frame: two characters side by side on a warm bed, strap above their heads.
shots.what_we_see: Frame 0 is MID-SHOVE. LEFT: the clean white panty-liner character (LP_LINER), about 55-60% of the underwear's height, leans ~15 deg into the underwear's side seam with a little motion smear on its edge, tab-hands braced. RIGHT: the plain black underwear character (LP_UNDIES, built from the 5 sample photos: no lace, no logo) stands upright on its leg openings, tilted ~8 deg away mid-rock. Its face sits on the upper front panel just under the waistband (eyes one finger-width below the seam, mouth above the leg-opening curve). Warm Cream duvet with soft folds fills the lower half, a folded Claret throw on the foot edge, Blush and cream pillows, a soft-focus wooden headboard, a lamp glowing top-right (2700K) and soft window fill from the left. Bright and warm, nothing dark, no person, no brands.
shots.motion_inside_shot: Three motion events, no cut. (1) 0.0-0.4s: the shove lands; the underwear rocks back and springs upright. (2) 0.3-1.0s: on the bell both bounce into a boxer's stance; the liner hops on its toes with tab-hands up like gloves, the underwear plants and lifts one brow. (3) 1.0-3.0s: slow dolly push-in 100->112% while the liner leans toward the lens on 'sneeze'; at ~2.7s the underwear's eyes slide to the liner. The edit starts 4-8 frames into the gen so the published frame 0 is already moving.
shots.on_screen_text: HOOK: Claret pill, cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, centred at ~20-28% height (the strap slot of 1691171645641479), on at frame 0 with no animate-in: 'Big sneeze. Little pee.' 0.3s: a Plum Ink 'VS' roundel with a Claret ring and cream type slams in between the fighters (~38-44%) on the bell. 1.6s: Warm Cream box, Plum Ink text, ~52-58%: 'What's the difference?' Persistent AI label (tiny, cream 80% on a Plum Ink 50% box, ~60% height, left): 'AI-generated. Not real customers.'
shots.vo_or_dialogue: LINER (higher, fussy, fast) 0.4-2.7s: “I'm what she grabs for the sneeze.” UNDERWEAR silent, mouth closed (reacts only).
shots.sfx: 0.1s muffled off-screen 'achoo' (audio only, no person). 0.3s single boxing-bell DING synced to the stance bounce. A dry comedy bed (pizzicato + brushed snare) enters on the bell. Soft whoosh under the push-in. Strip Veo's own ambience.
shots.cut_reason: One held hook shot (no top reference cuts inside 0-3s) with 3 motion events and 3 text events, so the frame changes roughly every 0.7s. Cut at 3.0s on the speaker change: the underwear answers.
shots.tool_rec: Nano Banana Pro start frame (Higgsfield, 9:16, 2k) on the approved bedroom plate with both reference elements, mouths closed. Then Veo 3.1 start-frame, 8s gen, keep 0.0-3.0s. pacing_check.broll_or_insert_share: 52% location hops + real-look inserts + poster freezes (17.2s), including 14% real-look product (4.5s: waistband stretch, leggings pull-up, washer). Two-shots are only 21% (6.8s); single-character bed angles are 15% (5.1s); the end card is 12% (3.9s). Non-two-shot coverage = 79%, against the brief's 25-35% floor.
vo_fit_issues: WHOLE SCRIPT: 80 spoken words. At the brief's 2.4 words/s that's ~33s; at a brisk cartoon pace (liner ~3.1 w/s, underwear ~2.5 w/s) with tight J-cuts it's 33.0s on this board, end card included. The script's 28s beat timings can't hold the lines. This board keeps every line (none changed) and runs 33.0s.

Script beat 1 (0-3s) holds 15 spoken words (~6s). On the board, only the liner's 7 words sit inside the hook shot (0.4-2.7s); the underwear's 8 words run 3.1-6.15s over the poster, the low-angle shot and the punch-in. So 'What's the difference?' is spoken at 5.0s, while the hook shows it as text at 1.6s for muted viewers.
Script beat 2 (3-7s) holds 15 words (~5.5s). On the board it spans 6.2-11.7s across 4 shots (handbag x2, drawer x2).
Script beat 4 (11-15s) holds 18 words (~6.5s staccato). On the board it spans 15.6-22.7s across 4 shots (high angle, ECU, OTS, bin).
Script beat 5 repeats beat 4's last line word for word ('…I go in the trash.' / 'So… I go in the trash.'). That's a tightening leftover.
Script beat 6 + end card hold 13 words (~5.5s). The liner's 'She knows where to find me' is moved onto the start of the end card (no words cut), so the card stays at 3.9s.

TRIM PATH TO ~29s (Nikita OK needed; no line has been changed without it). T1: cut the duplicate 'So… I go in the trash.' (S15 goes, -2.1s). T2: cut 'Same moment.' (the poster runs on the bell alone and 'I'm just underwear.' pre-laps over it, -0.8s); this also softens the implied 'same job as the liner' substitution read. Result ~30.1s, recommended. T3: cut 'Okay, fine.' (S11 goes and the confession opens on the ECU, -1.1s; total ~29.0s), not recommended because it's the confession's turn.
pacing_check.notes: How this beats the refs: 1691171645641479 parks on one bed angle for ~14s (4.8s average shot, 2 cuts in 3-10s). This board averages 1.65s, with 6 hard cuts + 1 edit punch-in in 3-10s, 5 locations (bed, tote, drawer, bin, washing line), 6 bed angles and 2 poster freezes, and no angle repeated on consecutive lines. It takes the room-per-line rule of the #4 Pixar winner 1400650075258672 (3.6s average) and adds real product at 11.7s, and it caps 1700150534480418's ~7s speaker holds at 3.0s. The hook is one held 3.0s shot with 3 motion events (shove, bell-bounce, push-in) and 3 text events, with an SFX on every cut in the first 10s. Deliberate exception: 16.7-18.3s and 24.8-25.4s are word-locked staccato beats inside the 10s+ section, and the rest of it runs 1.0-2.8s. LONG CUT (~45s, retargeting): restores any trimmed lines, adds the audio-only ACHOO flashback after the hook (ECU underwear deadpan, a new angle), and adds 'Panty liner: needs a bag. / Underwear: needs a drawer.' over a tote|drawer split. It also adds a second real-look under-leggings walk insert (side-on, walk only) and holds the end card +1s.
